actions: Take slow breaths and say out loud what happened.
Move only far enough to escape an immediate threat such as traffic, fire, falling rock, or rising water.
Mark where you stopped and note the time, weather, and last place you were certain of your location.
lessons.goal: Stop moving long enough to think clearly and avoid making the emergency larger.
lessons.title: Stop and Control Panic
warnings: Do not run downhill or follow water just because it appears to lead out.

actions: Look for traffic, fire, unstable terrain, weather, water, wildlife, and falling objects.
Check breathing, severe bleeding, confusion, and the ability to move safely.
Control the most urgent threat, then repeat the check after any move or major change.
lessons.goal: Find immediate threats and life-threatening injuries before working on comfort or travel.
lessons.title: Check Danger and Injuries
warnings: Do not enter a dangerous area to recover replaceable gear.

actions: Empty pockets and packs in one controlled place so nothing is lost.
Separate dry insulation, first aid, water treatment, light, ignition, navigation, and communication items.
Protect the most important items from rain, damage, and accidental use.
lessons.goal: Know exactly which tools, clothing, food, water, medicines, and signals are available.
lessons.title: Inventory What You Have
warnings: Do not scatter equipment while searching in darkness or bad weather.

actions: Treat breathing and severe bleeding first.
Prevent dangerous heat loss, heat gain, fire, flood, or traffic exposure next.
Then secure water, signaling, navigation, and food in the order current conditions require.
lessons.goal: Choose the next action from immediate threats, not from a fixed rule of threes.
lessons.title: Set Priorities for Conditions
warnings: A memorized priority list must change when the actual threat changes.

actions: Ask whether anyone knows your route and whether searchers are likely.
Compare the risks of staying with the terrain, distance, daylight, weather, injury, and certainty of any move.
If staying, make shelter and signals; if moving, leave a clear note and mark direction and time.
aliases: decide whether to stay or move
lessons.goal: Stay near the last known route unless remaining creates more danger or a known safe destination is close.
lessons.title: Decide Whether to Stay or Move
warnings: Do not move on a guess or separate a group without a clear rescue reason.

actions: Choose a safer site while there is enough light to inspect it.
Collect needed water and fuel before cold, fatigue, or darkness increases risk.
Place light, shoes, insulation, first aid, and signaling tools where they can be reached immediately.
lessons.goal: Finish shelter, warmth, water, and signals before darkness removes safe options.
lessons.title: Organize the First Night
warnings: Do not wait until dark to discover that the site floods, sheds branches, or lacks insulation.

actions: Notice thirst, dry mouth, headache, dark urine, dizziness, weakness, and reduced coordination.
Rest in shade, loosen excess layers, and drink safe water in manageable amounts.
Treat confusion, collapse, seizure, or inability to drink as an emergency.
lessons.goal: Reduce exertion and replace safe fluids before weakness or confusion becomes severe.
lessons.title: Recognize Dehydration
warnings: Do not force fluid into anyone who is not fully alert or cannot swallow.

actions: Check maps, valleys, drainage lines, springs, green vegetation, animal movement, and low ground.
Listen for flowing water and look for converging terrain rather than wandering randomly.
Travel during cooler hours and leave markers if a short water search takes you away from shelter.
lessons.goal: Search deliberately for water without spending more fluid and energy than the search can return.
lessons.title: Locate Likely Water
warnings: Do not enter steep ravines, unstable banks, caves, or fast water to reach a source.

actions: Prefer a known safe supply, then clearer moving water collected upstream from camps, livestock, roads, or waste.
Avoid water with fuel sheen, chemical smell, toxic algae, dead animals, mine drainage, or industrial runoff.
Collect where the bank is stable and you cannot be swept into the water.
lessons.goal: Use the least contaminated available source and still treat it for germs.
lessons.title: Choose the Safest Source
warnings: Boiling and ordinary filters cannot make chemically contaminated or salty water safe.

actions: Let cloudy water settle in a clean container.
Pour off the clearer layer or pass it through clean cloth or a coffee filter.
Keep dirty collection containers and hands away from the clean-water opening and cap.
lessons.goal: Remove sediment before the main treatment without mistaking clear water for safe water.
lessons.title: Collect and Prefilter Water
warnings: Prefiltering removes particles only; it does not reliably remove disease-causing organisms.

actions: Bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute.
Above 6,500 feet (about 1,980 metres), boil for 3 minutes.
Let it cool and store it in a clean, covered container without touching the inside of the cap.
lessons.goal: Use a rolling boil for the full recommended time, then prevent recontamination.
lessons.title: Boil Water Correctly
warnings: Boiling does not remove fuel, toxic chemicals, salt, or radioactive contamination.

actions: Read what the filter or purifier removes and check for damage or freezing.
Follow the maker's dose, water clarity, temperature, and contact-time instructions.
When boiling is unavailable, filter cloudy water and then disinfect it when the product permits.
lessons.goal: Follow the treatment product exactly and combine methods when one method misses important organisms.
lessons.title: Filter or Disinfect Water
warnings: Many backpacking filters do not remove viruses, and some disinfectants do not reliably kill every parasite.

actions: Use clean, covered containers and keep untreated and treated water clearly separate.
Travel in cooler hours, rest in shade, pace work, and loosen excess insulation before sweating heavily.
Drink available safe water and use normal food or directed electrolyte products during prolonged effort.
aliases: store water and reduce fluid loss
lessons.goal: Protect treated water and reduce sweating instead of dangerously withholding water.
lessons.title: Store Water and Reduce Fluid Loss
warnings: Do not drink seawater, urine, alcohol, or vehicle fluids for hydration.

actions: Check wind, dryness, overhead fuel, escape routes, local restrictions, and whether a stove or insulation can meet the need.
Choose a fire only if it can remain small, attended, and fully controlled.
Prepare water, soil, or another extinguishing method before ignition.
lessons.goal: Use fire only when its survival benefit exceeds wildfire, smoke, fuel, and legal risks.
lessons.title: Decide Whether Fire Is Safe
warnings: Never light a fire during a ban or where wind and dry fuel can carry sparks beyond control.

actions: Use an existing approved fire area when available.
Clear loose fuel to mineral soil for a safe distance suited to wind and conditions.
Look above for branches and around for roots, peat, dry grass, tents, vehicles, and fuel containers.
lessons.goal: Place the smallest useful fire on stable ground away from people, shelter, roots, and spreading fuel.
lessons.title: Choose a Fire Site
warnings: Do not build on peat, deep duff, roots, inside a tent, or beneath low branches.

actions: Prepare fine dry tinder that catches a flame or spark.
Add pencil-thin kindling, then finger-thick sticks, then larger fuel only after each size burns well.
Keep a protected reserve dry and gather enough to avoid leaving the fire unattended.
lessons.goal: Collect enough dry material in increasing sizes before striking the first spark.
lessons.title: Gather Tinder, Kindling, and Fuel
warnings: Do not strip live trees or collect material where local rules prohibit it.

actions: Prepare the complete tinder and kindling bundle before using a match, lighter, or ferro rod.
Block wind with your body or a safe barrier while preserving airflow.
Move the burning tinder into the fire lay and add fuel gradually.
lessons.goal: Shield the tinder and use the simplest reliable ignition method you already know.
lessons.title: Use Common Ignition Tools
warnings: Do not spill liquid fuel onto a flame or improvise with batteries unless the equipment is designed for it.

actions: Build a loose teepee, lean-to, or platform of kindling around the tinder.
Add only a few pieces at a time as the flame strengthens.
Keep the fire no larger than needed for warmth, boiling, cooking, or signaling.
lessons.goal: Keep airflow open and add fuel slowly enough that the flame is not smothered.
lessons.title: Build and Feed the Fire
warnings: A large fire consumes fuel quickly and is harder to control, extinguish, and shelter from wind.

actions: Work beneath a safe cover that cannot catch fire and isolate tinder from wet ground.
Split standing dead wood when legal to reach a drier center.
Build a small platform, use extra fine tinder, and add warmed kindling gradually.
lessons.goal: Protect the working area and expose dry inner wood instead of burning energy on soaked surfaces.
lessons.title: Start Fire in Wet Conditions
warnings: Do not hold wet fuel over flames where steam, collapse, or sparks can injure you.

actions: Burn fuel down, spread coals, add water, stir, and repeat until no heat remains.
Use soil only when water is unavailable and keep checking for heat below the surface.
Vent any approved stove or heater exactly as designed and keep combustion outside sleeping spaces.
lessons.goal: Attend the fire continuously and leave it cold enough to touch.
lessons.title: Prevent Wildfire and Fumes
warnings: Never sleep with an open flame, charcoal, stove, or engine exhaust in an enclosed shelter.

actions: Move away from flood channels, unstable slopes, cliff edges, exposed ridges, roads, and avalanche paths.
Check for dead trees, hanging branches, loose rock, rising-water marks, wildlife trails, and fire spread.
Choose natural wind protection with drainage and enough visibility for signals.
lessons.goal: Avoid hazards above, below, and around the site before building.
lessons.title: Choose a Shelter Site
warnings: Do not choose the lowest flat ground during rain or shelter beneath a dead tree.

actions: Use a sleeping pad, pack, spare clothing, dry vegetation where legal, or other dry material.
Build insulation thicker than it looks necessary because body weight compresses it.
Keep wet clothing and bare skin away from cold ground and replace crushed material as needed.
lessons.goal: Put dry insulation beneath the body before making the shelter larger or more comfortable.
lessons.title: Insulate From the Ground
warnings: Do not use toxic plants, thorny material, or wet insulation against skin.

actions: Choose solid anchors and run a ridgeline or supported edge without damaging trees.
Angle the tarp steeply enough to shed rain and lower the windward side.
Stake or weight corners, keep fabric away from flame, and add ground insulation.
lessons.goal: Pitch a small stable roof that blocks the main wind and sheds water away from the sleeping area.
lessons.title: Build a Tarp Shelter
warnings: Do not seal the shelter so tightly that condensation, stove fumes, or carbon monoxide accumulates.

actions: Choose a stable ridge pole and supports that cannot roll or collapse.
Make the enclosed space only large enough for the body and add a thick layer of dry debris over the frame.
Add a deep dry bed, block the entrance partly, and test the structure gently before entering.
lessons.goal: Use a strong frame and deep dry insulation when no carried shelter is available.
lessons.title: Build a Debris Shelter
warnings: Do not cut live vegetation or build where debris collection is prohibited; never use an unstable log as the main support.

actions: Choose a site away from avalanche paths, cornices, tree wells, and drifting snow.
Use a tent, snow trench, or snow structure only if you know it can remain stable and ventilated.
Mark the entrance, keep tools inside, and clear vents as snow falls.
lessons.goal: Block wind, stay dry, insulate deeply, and keep ventilation open.
lessons.title: Shelter in Cold or Snow
warnings: Snow shelters can collapse or trap carbon monoxide; never use a flame or stove without designed ventilation.

actions: In heat, create overhead shade, allow airflow, and avoid hot ground and enclosed vehicles.
In rain or wind, lower the profile, face the strong side into the weather, and route runoff away.
Adjust clothing and ventilation early so sweat or condensation does not soak insulation.
aliases: shelter from heat, sun, wind, and rain
lessons.goal: Use shade and airflow in heat, and wind and water barriers in cold rain.
lessons.title: Shelter From Heat, Sun, Wind, and Rain
warnings: A sealed shelter in sun can become dangerously hot even when outdoor air feels moderate.

actions: Tighten or loosen lines as fabric and weather change.
Keep light, shoes, insulation, first aid, and an exit path ready.
Set safe checks for rising water, snow load, wind, fire, or a sick person.
lessons.goal: Recheck anchors, drainage, ventilation, warmth, and hazards before sleep and after weather changes.
lessons.title: Maintain Shelter Overnight
warnings: Do not ignore new cracking trees, moving water, smoke, or changing wind because the shelter is already built.

actions: Estimate likely rescue time, weather, health, daylight, and food already available.
Choose only methods with a high chance of return and low injury risk.
Stop if gathering consumes water, warmth, navigation certainty, or signaling time.
aliases: decide whether food gathering is worth it
lessons.goal: Protect warmth, water, signaling, and rescue chances before spending energy to find food.
lessons.title: Decide Whether Food Gathering Is Worth It
warnings: Healthy adults can usually tolerate short food gaps better than dehydration, exposure, or injury.

actions: Count food and separate an emergency reserve.
Eat small planned amounts during necessary activity instead of finishing easy snacks early.
Keep food dry, sealed, and protected from animals and contamination.
lessons.goal: Protect existing calories and use them to support warmth, decisions, and necessary work.
lessons.title: Manage Carried Food
warnings: Do not restrict food from children, people with diabetes, or anyone with a medical need without appropriate guidance.

actions: Use carried food or other lower-risk options first.
Treat look-alike species, mushrooms, berries, roots, and water plants as unknown unless already known with certainty.
Keep unknown material away from children and food-preparation surfaces.
lessons.goal: Eat wild plants or mushrooms only when identification is certain from prior expert knowledge, not from text or guesswork.
lessons.title: Reject Unknown Plants and Fungi
warnings: TrailGuard does not identify edible plants or mushrooms; small taste tests do not prove safety.

actions: Prefer stationary, close-to-camp options that do not require dangerous climbing, swimming, or weapons.
Fish only where legal and only if you have suitable gear and safe access to the bank.
Mark your route, limit time, and stop before weather, darkness, or fatigue worsens.
lessons.goal: Gather food only with methods you already know, can use legally, and can perform without injury or getting lost.
lessons.title: Use Only Low-Risk Procurement
warnings: Do not eat unfamiliar animals, shellfish, insects, or plants merely because another animal ate them.

actions: Wash or sanitize hands and keep raw material away from ready-to-eat food.
Cook animal food thoroughly through the center using a thermometer when available.
Discard food with unsafe storage, chemical contact, spoilage, or uncertain origin.
lessons.goal: Prevent illness by separating raw food, cooking thoroughly, and keeping hands and tools clean.
lessons.title: Cook and Handle Food Safely
warnings: Smoke, color, smell, or a brief sear does not prove meat or fish is safe.

actions: Keep a clean camp and collect every crumb, wrapper, and scented item.
Use approved canisters, lockers, or vehicle storage where required; otherwise use the safest locally recommended method.
Cook and eat away from sleeping areas and never feed wildlife.
lessons.goal: Separate food and scented items from sleeping space and follow local storage rules.
lessons.title: Protect Food From Wildlife
warnings: Food storage rules and animal behavior vary by region; check local guidance before travel.

actions: Stop as soon as landmarks, trail, or position stop matching expectations.
Mark the spot without damaging the environment and record time and direction of travel.
Review the last certain point, recent turns, terrain, distance, and elevation before moving.
aliases: stop and mark the last known point
lessons.goal: Prevent the search area from growing while you reconstruct where navigation failed.
lessons.title: Stop and Mark the Last Known Point
warnings: Do not keep walking simply to feel productive.

actions: Identify north, contour lines, water, roads, trails, and major landmarks.
Rotate the map until mapped features line up with the same features around you.
Use at least two reliable features to estimate position and confirm it as you move.
lessons.goal: Turn the map to match the ground before choosing a route.
lessons.title: Orient a Map
warnings: A map on a phone is only useful if the correct area is downloaded and the device has power.

actions: Keep the compass level and away from vehicles, speakers, magnets, and large metal objects.
Set or read the bearing using the map and account for local declination when precision matters.
Choose a visible landmark on the bearing, walk to it, and recheck.
lessons.goal: Use the compass to hold a known direction, not to invent a destination.
lessons.title: Use a Compass
warnings: A precise bearing toward the wrong destination is still wrong; verify with terrain and map.

actions: Look for the shape and direction of large features before relying on small details.
Use handrails such as a trail, ridge, or shoreline and identify a catching feature beyond the destination.
Check that elevation, distance, and travel time agree with the expected route.
lessons.goal: Match ridges, valleys, slopes, water, and human features to the map continuously.
lessons.title: Read Terrain and Landmarks
warnings: Streams and valleys can lead into cliffs, waterfalls, canyons, and dense terrain rather than safety.

actions: Confirm recognizable footprints, markers, junctions, or terrain before committing.
Mark progress and turn around immediately if the track becomes uncertain.
Preserve enough daylight and energy to return to shelter and signals.
lessons.goal: Return only when the route behind you is known, short, and safer than staying.
lessons.title: Backtrack Safely
warnings: Do not follow isolated footprints or game trails as proof of the correct route.

actions: Observe the sun's general movement and changing shadows over time.
Compare the rough direction with terrain, map, and the last known route.
Treat cloud, season, latitude, terrain, and time uncertainty as large error sources.
aliases: use sun and shadow as rough aids
lessons.goal: Use natural direction clues only to support a map, compass, or known terrain—not as precise navigation.
lessons.title: Use Sun and Shadow as Rough Aids
warnings: Do not travel toward a guessed direction from one shadow or a remembered survival trick.

actions: Avoid unnecessary travel at night, in severe weather, or when injury or fatigue is worsening.
For a crossing, look for a wide shallow section away from rapids, falls, and hazards downstream.
Unbuckle pack waist and chest straps, face upstream, and use a sturdy pole only when the crossing is clearly manageable.
lessons.goal: Choose routes that preserve footing, visibility, and a safe return.
lessons.title: Travel and Cross Water Safely
warnings: Turn back when water is swift, deep, rising, very cold, or the exit cannot be seen; never tie yourself to a crossing rope.

actions: Try the local emergency number; in the United States and Canada use 911 when service exists.
Give location, problem, people, injuries, supplies, weather, and planned actions.
Preserve battery, keep the device warm and dry, and follow dispatcher or beacon instructions.
lessons.goal: Send a short complete rescue message whenever a phone, beacon, radio, or satellite device can connect.
lessons.title: Use Emergency Communication
warnings: Do not depend on a phone alone; coverage and location reporting can fail.

actions: Give three strong blasts, pause, listen, and repeat at regular intervals.
Move only to a nearby safe opening or ridge if it clearly improves the signal.
Keep the whistle attached to clothing so it remains available after a fall or lost pack.
lessons.goal: Use repeated whistle blasts that travel farther than shouting and cost less energy.
lessons.title: Signal With a Whistle
warnings: Do not blow continuously until exhausted or unable to hear a reply.

actions: Use a signal mirror's sighting aid or move the reflection slowly across the target.
At night, flash a light in groups of three and preserve battery between signal periods.
Use bright fabric or reflective material to make the signaling position easier to find.
lessons.goal: Aim reflected sun or repeated light flashes toward aircraft, boats, roads, and search teams.
lessons.title: Use Mirrors and Lights
warnings: Never aim a laser at an aircraft or vehicle.

actions: Use an open area visible from likely search directions without entering an exposed hazard.
Make an SOS, X, arrow, or three repeated shapes using bright fabric, logs, rocks, or disturbed snow.
Make each line broad and much larger than a standing person, then keep the center clear.
lessons.goal: Create large high-contrast shapes that can be distinguished from natural terrain.
lessons.title: Make Visible Ground Signals
warnings: Do not dismantle shelter or scatter essential insulation to build a signal.

actions: Prepare the site, extinguishing material, and escape path before ignition.
Use three small fires or add damp green material only after a stable fire is controlled and local conditions allow.
Extinguish fully if wind rises, the signal is no longer needed, or control weakens.
aliases: use smoke or fire only when safe
lessons.goal: Create a controlled visible signal without starting a wildfire or poisoning shelter occupants.
lessons.title: Use Smoke or Fire Only When Safe
warnings: Do not light a signal fire during a ban, extreme fire weather, or where sparks can escape.

actions: Choose regular listening and signaling times around daylight, aircraft activity, or known search plans.
Keep a written log of attempts, replies, weather, and any movement.
Leave a durable note with time and direction if safety forces you to relocate.
lessons.goal: Repeat signals when searchers are most likely while preserving energy and batteries.
lessons.title: Set a Signaling Schedule
warnings: Do not miss a reply by making constant noise or wearing headphones.

actions: Check for danger before touching the person and use protective barriers when available.
Check responsiveness, open the airway as trained, and look for normal breathing and severe bleeding.
Call or send for help; begin CPR and use an AED when indicated by current training and the device prompts.
aliases: assess the patient and cpr need
lessons.goal: Make the scene safe, check responsiveness and normal breathing, and start the appropriate emergency response.
lessons.title: Assess the Patient and CPR Need
warnings: Gasping is not normal breathing; do not delay emergency activation for a long examination.

actions: Expose the wound and press firmly with gauze or clean cloth.
Maintain pressure and add material without repeatedly lifting the first pad to check.
For uncontrolled life-threatening limb bleeding, apply a commercial tourniquet according to training and record the time.
lessons.goal: Apply immediate firm pressure and escalate to a tourniquet for life-threatening limb bleeding when trained and equipped.
lessons.title: Control Severe Bleeding
warnings: Do not loosen a tourniquet after application; obtain emergency evacuation as quickly as possible.

actions: Lay the person in the safest comfortable position unless breathing or injury requires otherwise.
Control bleeding, keep the person dry and insulated, and reassure them.
Monitor breathing and alertness, and arrange urgent evacuation.
lessons.goal: Control the cause, protect temperature, and evacuate urgently when circulation or mental status worsens.
lessons.title: Treat for Shock
warnings: Do not give food or drink to someone with reduced alertness, vomiting, or likely surgery.

actions: For a wound, control bleeding, rinse with the cleanest available safe water, and cover with a clean dressing.
For a thermal burn, remove the heat source and cool with cool clean running water when available.
Remove rings or tight items before swelling and arrange evacuation for deep, large, chemical, electrical, airway, face, hand, foot, or genital burns.
lessons.goal: Stop ongoing damage, cool or clean appropriately, cover, and watch for infection or deeper injury.
lessons.title: Care for Wounds and Burns
warnings: Do not put ice, grease, fuel, soil, or unverified remedies on a burn or wound.

actions: Keep the person still and support the injured area in the position found unless circulation is absent or the location is dangerous.
Check feeling, warmth, color, and pulse beyond the injury before and after splinting.
Pad a splint above and below the injury without forcing the limb straight.
lessons.goal: Prevent further movement, check circulation, and evacuate when a serious bone, joint, head, neck, or back injury is possible.
lessons.title: Stabilize Fractures and Spine Injuries
warnings: Do not move a suspected spine injury unless needed for airway, CPR, or immediate scene safety.

actions: Move to shade, remove excess clothing, and cool skin with water and airflow.
Give cool safe fluids only if the person is fully alert and can swallow.
For confusion, seizure, collapse, or very hot skin, cool aggressively and activate emergency evacuation.
lessons.goal: Stop exertion, cool early, and treat confusion or collapse as heat stroke.
lessons.title: Treat Heat Illness
warnings: Do not give fever medicine or force fluids into an altered person.

actions: Move out of wind and wet, replace wet clothing, and insulate above and below.
Warm the chest, neck, armpits, and groin with wrapped warm packs or shared body heat.
Protect frostbitten tissue from pressure and refreezing; evacuate serious cases.
lessons.goal: Stop heat loss, handle gently, and rewarm the body core without burning skin.
lessons.title: Treat Hypothermia and Frostbite
warnings: Do not rub frostbite, use direct fire, give alcohol, or thaw tissue that may refreeze.

actions: Move away from the animal, insects, plant, chemical, or contaminated area without creating another injury.
For anaphylaxis, help use prescribed epinephrine immediately and activate emergency response.
For poisoning, preserve the container or description and contact the local poison service when communication exists.
aliases: respond to bites, stings, allergy, and poison
lessons.goal: End exposure, support breathing, use prescribed emergency medicine, and seek expert help.
lessons.title: Respond to Bites, Stings, Allergy, and Poison
warnings: Do not cut or suck a snakebite, apply ice or an electric shock, or make the person walk unnecessarily.

actions: Leave ridges, peaks, open water, open fields, and isolated tall objects immediately.
If no safe building or vehicle exists, spread a group apart and move toward lower terrain away from water and tall isolated trees.
Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before leaving safe shelter.
lessons.goal: Reach a substantial building or hard-topped vehicle; no outdoor place is fully safe.
lessons.title: Act During Lightning
warnings: A tent, cave entrance, picnic shelter, cliff overhang, or isolated tree is not reliable lightning protection.

actions: Add dry layers and protect head, hands, feet, and the body core.
Get off snow or cold ground and build wind protection.
Eat available food, drink safe fluids, and monitor each person for confusion, stumbling, or fading shivering.
lessons.goal: Stay dry, block wind, add insulation, and act before shivering or coordination worsens.
lessons.title: Survive Severe Cold
warnings: Stopping shivering while still cold can mean severe hypothermia, not recovery.

actions: Stop or slow activity and move to shade during the hottest period.
Loosen excess clothing, wet skin when water is available, and create airflow.
Drink safe water and monitor for headache, nausea, cramps, confusion, or collapse.
lessons.goal: Reduce heat production and increase shade, airflow, and safe hydration before illness begins.
lessons.title: Survive Extreme Heat
warnings: A parked vehicle or sealed shelter can become lethal in heat; confusion or collapse requires rapid cooling and emergency help.

actions: Leave washes, stream beds, narrow canyons, low crossings, and flood-marked campsites.
Move uphill by the safest available route without crossing moving water.
Watch distant weather because flooding can arrive from rain outside your location.
lessons.goal: Move early to higher ground when heavy rain, rising water, or a warning affects a drainage or canyon.
lessons.title: Escape Flash-Flood Risk
warnings: Never enter moving floodwater on foot or in a vehicle; depth and road condition cannot be judged reliably.

actions: Call emergency services when possible and follow official evacuation routes.
Move toward a large cleared area, water edge, road, or already burned area when that is the safest reachable option.
Cover nose and mouth from ash, stay low in cleaner air, and keep skin covered.
lessons.goal: Move away from fire spread and heavy smoke while avoiding steep, fuel-filled escape routes.
lessons.title: Respond to Wildfire and Smoke
warnings: Do not try to outrun a fast fire uphill or shelter in dense vegetation, a tent, or a vehicle surrounded by burning fuel.

actions: Move away from ridges, cliffs, dead trees, hanging branches, power lines, and unsecured objects.
Lower and reinforce shelter, secure loose gear, and keep an exit clear.
After the storm, reassess floodwater, unstable trees, cold exposure, and route damage.
lessons.goal: Leave exposed and falling-object zones before wind or precipitation peaks.
lessons.title: Handle Wind and Storms
warnings: Do not shelter in a dry stream bed or beneath damaged trees to escape wind.

actions: Do not approach, feed, surround, or block the animal's escape route.
Back away calmly when appropriate and make your presence known without running.
Use approved bear spray only as trained and carry it where it is immediately reachable in bear country.
aliases: respond to bears and large animals
lessons.goal: Create distance, avoid surprise, protect food, and follow species-specific local guidance.
lessons.title: Respond to Bears and Large Animals
warnings: Bear, moose, bison, cougar, and other animal responses differ; never treat one universal tactic as correct for every species.

actions: Watch where hands and feet go around rocks, logs, brush, and stored gear.
Wear footwear and use repellent, nets, and clothing appropriate to local disease risks.
Shake out clothing and bedding and keep camp away from nests or obvious animal paths.
Use required canisters, lockers, or approved vehicle storage; clean crumbs, waste, cookware, and scented items before sleep.
aliases: avoid snakes, insects, and food raids
lessons.goal: Reduce animal contact, inspect before reaching, and secure every food or scented item.
lessons.title: Avoid Snakes, Insects, and Food Raids
warnings: Do not handle or attempt to kill a snake; many bites occur during handling.
Improvised food hangs are not accepted everywhere and can fail with local wildlife; follow site-specific rules.

actions: Slow smoothly, signal, and move fully out of the travel lane when the vehicle remains controllable.
Apply the parking brake, select Park or a low gear, turn on hazard lights, and assess whether staying inside is safer.
Exit away from traffic only when needed and move behind a substantial barrier when available.
lessons.goal: Protect people from traffic, fire, slope, and weather before diagnosing the vehicle.
lessons.title: Stop and Secure the Scene
warnings: Never work in a live traffic lane; move well away from smoke, fire, fuel smell, or a damaged high-voltage battery.

actions: Note warning lights, sounds, smells, leaks, weather, location, fuel or charge, and occupants' condition.
Use the owner's manual for the exact vehicle and avoid repeated start attempts.
If sheltering, make the vehicle visible, conserve power and fuel, and send location and condition when possible.
aliases: diagnose and decide whether to stay
lessons.goal: Stay with the vehicle unless it is unsafe or a known reachable destination clearly offers better survival odds.
lessons.title: Diagnose and Decide Whether to Stay
warnings: Do not walk into unknown distance, heat, cold, flood, or darkness without a clear destination and route.

actions: Set the parking brake, secure occupants, read the owner's procedure, and gather the correct spare and tools.
Chock a wheel, loosen fasteners slightly before lifting, and use only the marked jack point.
Fit the spare, tighten in the stated pattern, lower the vehicle, retighten, and obey temporary-spare limits.
lessons.goal: Lift a vehicle only on firm level ground outside traffic and only at the manufacturer-specified points.
lessons.title: Change a Tire Safely
warnings: Never put any part of your body under a vehicle supported only by a jack; do not lift on soft ground, a slope, or beside fast traffic.

actions: Inspect for swelling, leaks, freezing, damage, smoke, or incorrect voltage; stop if any is present.
Turn vehicles and accessories off and connect clamps in the exact owner-manual order using designated points.
Keep clamps apart and clear of moving parts; disconnect in the stated reverse order after a successful start.
lessons.goal: Jump-start only when the owner's manual permits it and both systems and connection points are identified.
lessons.title: Use a 12-Volt Jump Start
warnings: Never jump an unidentified, damaged, frozen, or leaking battery, and never connect to hybrid or EV high-voltage components.

actions: Switch the vehicle off and locate the correct fuse diagram in the owner's manual.
Remove only the named fuse with the supplied tool and replace it only with the same type and rating.
Stop if the new fuse fails or if wiring is hot, damaged, wet, or smells burned.
aliases: check fuses and basic electrical faults
lessons.goal: Limit checks to owner-serviceable fuses and obvious 12-volt connections documented by the vehicle maker.
lessons.title: Check Fuses and Basic Electrical Faults
warnings: Never bypass a fuse, install a higher rating, probe airbags, or touch orange high-voltage wiring.

actions: Turn off air conditioning and move to a safe stopping place without pushing a badly overheating engine.
Switch off, keep clear of steam or leaking fluid, and wait until fully cool.
Check only owner-serviceable reservoirs and approved fluids; stop driving if the warning returns or a leak continues.
aliases: respond to overheating or fluid loss
lessons.goal: Reduce load, stop safely, switch off, and let the system cool before any owner-approved check.
lessons.title: Respond to Overheating or Fluid Loss
warnings: Never open a hot radiator or pressurized cap, pour cold water on a hot engine, or touch unknown leaking fluid.

actions: Clear snow, mud, or sand from the driven wheels and ensure the exhaust outlet is open.
Straighten wheels, use traction material, and apply gentle power without prolonged wheelspin.
Stop repeated attempts if the vehicle sinks, overheats, loses traction equipment, or approaches unstable terrain.
aliases: recover from snow, mud, or sand
lessons.goal: Prevent exhaust poisoning and vehicle damage before attempting gentle self-recovery.
lessons.title: Recover From Snow, Mud, or Sand
warnings: Never stand in the path of a spinning tire, tensioned strap, winch line, or rocking vehicle.

actions: After a crash, flood, fire, battery warning, unusual heat, popping, smoke, or sweet/solvent odor, switch off if safe and move away.
Call emergency services, identify the vehicle as electric or hybrid, and display a bright signal without returning to a dangerous vehicle.
Use only the owner's approved towing method and tell responders if the battery was submerged or damaged.
If the vehicle is undamaged and used as shelter, clear snow from the exhaust, conserve power, ventilate safely, and keep an exit usable.
lessons.goal: Assume damaged high-voltage components are energized; keep people away and use the safe vehicle as shelter only when conditions allow.
lessons.title: Handle EV/Hybrid Damage and Shelter
warnings: Never touch orange cables, open the traction battery, approach leaking battery material, or park a damaged battery vehicle near structures or combustibles.
Never run an engine in an enclosed area or where exhaust can enter the cabin.
